note: Seventh and final round. Commit 956c8cd added a net/http entry to internal/run/findings.go's clientKnobPatterns (Client.Timeout, Transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout, Transport.DialContext, Transport.TLSHandshakeTimeout, Transport.MaxIdleConnsPerHost). Commit addcee5 taught internal/detect to read manifests from each compose service's own build context, not just the project root, via a new detectServiceManifests + Dep.ClientRefs. Restored fixtures to their natural per-service go.mod layout (removed the project-root go.mod workaround from case 3 and case 7). Re-ran the whole corpus via `make eval` (now wired to evals/run_case.sh, rewritten this round into a full corpus runner with a case-8 gate). Finding, reported rather than routed around: cases 1, 2 and 5 still carry no candidates, for a reason neither commit reaches -- see case1_no_timeout below.

case1_no_timeout.candidates_STILL_missing_why: Verified directly (a throwaway program linking internal/detect against this fixture's compose file, run and discarded -- not committed): detect.System.Deps is empty for this stack; the only entry is a Gaps line, 'unrecognized image e1-case1-dep:latest (service dep) -- classify it in torture.yaml'. Two independent reasons compound: (1) 'dep' is a custom image outside detect's closed R-DET-9 vocabulary (postgres*/redis*/kafka*/etc.), so it never becomes a detect.Dep at all -- unchanged by either of this round's commits, since both only add to what a RECOGNIZED dependency's client library can be. depForTarget(deps, "dep:9090") returns nil regardless of what's in clientKnobPatterns. (2) Independently, even a recognized target's manifest scan could never have surfaced net/http anyway: internal/detect/lockfile.go's goClientPatterns table (the list of import-path -> R-DET-9-type mappings that gates what a manifest scan can attach a Dep) has no net/http entry, and go.mod's own "require" lines never list a stdlib package like net/http in the first place -- confirmed empirically for checkout-api's own (empty, no requires) go.mod. The new net/http row lives only in internal/run/findings.go's clientKnobPatterns (what knobs to name once a client is already known), not in internal/detect's own recognition table (whether net/http can be discovered as a client at all). Both gaps are structural, in internal/detect and internal/run respectively, both out of this task's edit scope. Reported, not fixed.

case6_unbounded_queue.defect: Unbounded in-memory queue drained far slower than it fills
case6_unbounded_queue.candidates_reason: Correctly still none, re-confirmed this round: an in-process unbounded queue is backed by no third-party client library, so detect.System has nothing to find and nothing honest to name.
case6_unbounded_queue.fixture_note: Tightened this round for reliability: the original 24m mem_limit was flaky (a 1MB-per-item queue oscillated at ~98% memory under GC pressure rather than reliably crossing the OOM threshold -- Go's GC, reclaiming already-drained slices as pressure rose, sometimes kept the process just under the cgroup limit). Raised the chunk size to 4MB and tightened mem_limit to 12m; 3/3 repeat runs now reliably OOM-kill (confirmed via docker inspect .State.OOMKilled=true each time). This is a reliability fix to the fixture's calibration, not a change to the planted defect (still an uncapped queue with no backpressure).

case7_cache_stampede.defect: Cache-aside read with a short TTL and no stampede protection
case7_cache_stampede.candidates_reason: Confirmed working with the fixture's natural layout this round (go.mod under api/, no workaround). Honestly limited: none of these knobs actually fixes a stampede (that needs application-level locking/singleflight, which no client-library knob table could ever name) -- Candidate.Source carries the '(no active fault -- detected client, not a diagnosis)' caveat precisely so this isn't overread.

case4_nonidempotent_consumer.reason: Needs a message broker, a Kafka REST Proxy-compatible endpoint, consumer-group semantics, and -broker-url wiring -- materially more infrastructure than the other five cases. Out of every round's budget so far. Unmeasured, not faked.
